title: How Does Killing Surviving Mutants Help Detect Real Bugs with Assertion Generation? A Controlled Experiment
venue: Proceedings of the ACM on software engineering.
year_venue: 2026 ISSTA; verified against official first-author publications page and paper PDF
datasets: Defects4J 3.0.1: paper states 854 bugs/17 subjects in corpus; after excluding Mockito and Closure, studies 642 real-bug versions across 15 subjects. The controlled mutant analysis focuses on 104 bugs with revealability gaps.
models: No LLM; deterministic assertion augmentation + Major mutation testing.
artifact_url: https://github.com/spideruci/Defects4j_for_Coupling_Effect_Analysis_Through_Killing_Surviving_Mutants; paper cites Zenodo DOI 10.5281/zenodo.21328338; GitHub README links prebuilt Docker example archive DOI 10.5281/zenodo.21013232.
input_setting: Remove developer triggering tests to construct bug-ignorant suite T; generate Major mutants on fixed version; use passing tests and compare state collected on fixed vs mutant versions; add one localized assertion and validate it passes fixed/fails faulty. For real-bug analysis, directly compare fixed and buggy versions. Not issue-report input, root-cause localization, or LLM test generation.
reproduction_grade: B (conditional full-study reproduction; documented Docker/CI examples make smoke reproduction feasible)
concept_hook: High: revealability-gap classification and mutation-derived behavioral assertions on Defects4J, but not issue-level root-cause diagnosis.
limitation: Full paper reports 1,177 experimental hours; paper DOI and README Docker archive Zenodo records differ and exact full dataset archive is unresolved.
